mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increase and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE increase and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in real GDP over two consecutive quarters signals a strong demand environment, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the GDP is increasing, or if the correlation between GDP growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% over a month signals a supply shock, which leads to increased costs and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO decrease and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts by more than 5% over two months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which boosts related industries and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between HOUST increase and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and the CPI is increasing by more than 0.3% per month, the combination signals an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary environment with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the interaction effect between FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.2% in the same month, it signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the interaction effect between PAYEMS and UNRATE on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in real retail and food services sales over three consecutive months signals a strong consumer demand environment, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS is increasing, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
